answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity post a stake that is burned if the identity cheats, and require a long reputation climb before it can hold real power. A newcomer starts at the haven of low-trust, low-value work, earning its way toward the summit of higher-value tasks only after a history of honest attestations. At the zenith of trust, an agent can vouch for others, but a vouch that endorses a cheater costs the voucher its own stake, so creating a hundred fake identities means funding a hundred deposits and a hundred slow climbs — far costlier than the fraud is worth.
